name: Developer loop terminated → run the structural floors (check_floors)
description:
The floors station (design R1, group 5). When Amelia's bounded dev loop TERMINATES (success or failed), run semdev's deterministic structural floors over her authored diff — did she author a test at all, is it vacuous, did she ship a stub, does the source parse, did she 'test' only a mock, and (H1) did she author ANY declared target. check_floors also MIRRORS the routing inputs onto its own loop (route.passed = the run's measurement, fail-closed 'false' if absent; route.rejected = its aggregate; route.attempt.0 = the append-mirror of task.attempt.0) so the floors ROUTE (06a-d) can fire on them (a rule reads only the firing entity's triples, and the route rules fire on this floors loop). G2: this fires no lifecycle transition; check_floors measures + mirrors, the route rules decide.

TRIGGER = the DEVELOPER loop's TERMINAL, not a measure loop (measure moved INTO Amelia's loop, R2). It fires on agent.loop.role=developer (stamped at spawn) AND agent.loop.outcome ne "" (stamped at completion — present iff the loop terminated, for BOTH success and failed). Gating on outcome-present (not outcome=success) is deliberate: a failed loop (max-iteration cap) is still a completed attempt the route must handle (retry/escalate on the harness-stamped facts, R2) — routing does not trust the loop's success/failure, it reads measurement.result + floor.finding. Each attempt mints a FRESH developer loop, so this re-fires per attempt for free.

RUN BINDING: run_scope=inherit reads the developer loop's agent.run and binds the check_floors loop's RunID to the same run, so check_floors resolves THIS run's checkout (the bytes Amelia committed) and reads its measurement/attempt facts for the mirror.

ROLE = coordinator (design roster: Sarah owns the harness tools; check_floors is NOT in Amelia's loop — it runs in its own forced single-turn coordinator loop, like project_tasks/provision). tool_choice=function forces check_floors and the allowlist scopes the loop to it; the loop calls it and StopLoops, writing floor.finding.* (run) + the route.* mirror (loop). check_floors takes only task_index (G3).

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps dev.floors_dispatched=$entity.instance on the DEVELOPER loop (the firing entity), guarded by dev.floors_dispatched length_eq 0. House pattern (publish_agent is not idempotent; role+outcome stay stamped, so without this a replay would re-spawn a duplicate floors loop). Marker stamped BEFORE the publish. A fresh developer loop per attempt carries no marker, so floors re-run per attempt for free.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt: SEMDEV — the developer's bounded dev loop terminated. Run the structural floors on the authored diff: call check_floors with task_index 0. The harness runs the deterministic floors (tests-must-exist, vacuous-test, stub, source-build, anti-mock, presence) over the run's checkout and records the findings, and mirrors the routing inputs onto this loop for the floors route — you supply no verdict. Calling check_floors completes your turn.

metadata.station: check_floors — run the structural floors on the developer-loop terminal (R1, group 5)
metadata.trigger_rationale: fires on the DEVELOPER loop's terminal (role=developer stamped at spawn; outcome ne "" stamped at completion — present for both success and failed). Routing keys on the harness facts, not the loop outcome, so floors run on any terminal. Replaces the old measure-loop chain (measure moved in-loop, R2).
metadata.role_rationale: coordinator (Sarah's harness tool; check_floors runs in a forced single-turn loop, NOT Amelia's multi-turn loop). tool_choice=function:check_floors + a scoped [check_floors] allowlist forces the call.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the LOOP-scoped dev.floors_dispatched marker + length_eq 0 guard, stamped BEFORE the publish. A fresh developer loop per attempt re-arms floors.
metadata.chain_note: check_floors mirrors route.passed/route.rejected/route.attempt.0 onto ITS loop; the floors route (06a advance / 06b not_clean / 06c retry / 06d escalate) fires on those mirror facts (design R1 — the rule-native routing that replaced check_gate).
